A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we find pre-trained word embeddings are useful in the following cases: 1) when the training set is very small, 2) when the training data is noisy, and 3) when the training and test sets are drawn from different domains.

pre-trained word embeddings can be useful for NMT when: 1) the source language is low resource, 2) the target language is high resource, 3) the target language has a rich morphology, and 4) when there is a large amount of monolingual data available.

pre-trained word embeddings help NMT systems only when the following conditions are met: (a) the training corpus is too small to train a large NMT system, (b) the embeddings are trained on a sufficiently large corpus of the same language, and (c) the NMT system is not trained to use word embeddings in a task-specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pre-trained word embeddings can be useful for NMT, but only in certain scenarios.
